affiliations: Copenhagen Business School - CBS Law

detail.title: The Case for an EU Cap on Interest on Underpaid Tax: Protecting the Internal Market

publicationDetails.detailsText: INTERTAX, Volume 52, Issue 1

detail.abstract: This article examines whether the differences in the calculation of interest on underpaid taxes among EU Member States could conflict with or impact the functioning of the EU internal market. The analysis indicates that such a conflict exists, and that an EU minimum standard protecting taxpayers' rights is justified to remedy this while harmonizing the rules on interest accrual entirely would likely exceed the limits of the proportionality principle. The article's starting point is the recent Danish Supreme Court ruling on beneficial ownership which recommends that the Danish legislator review national rules on interest accrual in cases of prolonged tax proceedings and consider a remedy that allows disputed amounts to be deposited with tax authorities. It evaluates the international and EU legal frameworks addressing this issue and compares interest accrual rules between Member States. The article finds that these legal frameworks offer insufficient guidance. It also discusses the Danish Supreme Court's suggested remedy and asserts that it is ineffective and inefficient. Furthermore, this study demonstrates that it is not suitable as an EU minimum standard, and the latter should instead be designed as a maximum percentage of the disputed amount. This relatively simple approach is a suitable manner for realizing the intended objective as it would incentivize taxpayers to pay their tax bills on time while safeguarding their fundamental human rights wherever they are established in the EU. Moreover, it would prevent placing undue administrative burdens on either taxpayers or tax administrations and would not impede Member States' abilities to design their tax administrative procedures to fit their national tax systems and practices.

title: Euro Area Inflation and Unemployment: Phillips Curve and Forecasting
affiliations: Sabanci University, University of Texas at Austin - Department of Economics and North Carolina State University

detail.title: Euro Area Inflation and Unemployment: Phillips Curve and Forecasting
detail.abstract: We study Euro Area inflation and unemployment dynamics by addressing the identification challenges inherent to estimating the Phillips curve and providing new frameworks and results for inflation forecasting. Phillips curve slope estimation is challenging due to the simultaneity between monetary policy and economic conditions that biases OLS estimates downward. To overcome this challenge, we adopt a panel local projection IV framework. We estimate the cumulative impacts of monetary policy shocks on inflation and unemployment over a given horizon, where we use U.S. monetary policy shocks as IVs to ensure a causal interpretation of our results. We show that the policy trade-off identified through this panel IV estimation of the Phillips curve relationship is not just qualitatively, but also quantitatively, different from OLS estimation. We find no evidence that this trade-off has changed recently in the post-pandemic period. Finally, we provide novel tools for inflation forecasting based on the panel Phillips curve model. We document that panel data models yield accurate one-year ahead forecasts for 17 member states in the 2009-2023 period and clearly outperform the commonly used, naïve single-country models.

title: Feeding the Poor: How Trade Liberalization Reduced Caloric Poverty in Peru
affiliations: Universidad Nacional Mayor de San Marcos

detail.title: Feeding the Poor: How Trade Liberalization Reduced Caloric Poverty in Peru
detail.abstract: While Peru's trade liberalization reduced monetary poverty from 58% to 20% between 2004 and 2019, caloric poverty stagnated at 25-35%. This divergence poses a puzzle: did trade fail to improve nutrition, or do aggregates mask heterogeneous effects? I exploit the 2009 US-Peru Free Trade Agreement as a natural experiment, using shift-share instrumental variables that interact pre-FTA regional production structures with sector-specific tariff reductions. Analyzing 1.5 million household observations from 2004-2023, I develop a dynamic general equilibrium model linking trade shocks to nutrition through income, price, commercialization, and fiscal channels. Trade liberalization substantially reduced caloric poverty in exposed regions: a one percentage point tariff reduction decreased poverty by 1.5 percentage points and raised real food expenditure by 9%. Effects were strikingly progressive-rural households experienced substantially larger poverty reductions than urban areas, and Indigenous populations gained more than non-Indigenous groups. Market forces (export wages, import competition, commercialization) dominated welfare gains, accounting for 85% of effects versus 15redistribution. These findings show trade generates progressive nutritional gains even under weak institutions when comparative advantage aligns with vulnerable populations.

title: Aspects of Combating Corruption in Institutions of Higher Education of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine

detail.title: Aspects of Combating Corruption in Institutions of Higher Education of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the specific forms, causes, and effective means of combating corruption in higher education institutions under the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine. The author identifies two fundamental approaches: creating incentive conditions for honest employment in academia and enforcing strict punitive measures against corrupt behavior. The study highlights the impact of corruption on student motivation, the quality of legal education, and the broader social implications in a time of war. Emphasis is placed on increasing transparency and accountability; strengthening internal and external controls; improving social protection for educators; implementing anonymous assessments; and promoting patriotic and legal education of future law enforcement officers. The research concludes that persistent corruption in university environments perpetuates detrimental attitudes into wider society, making systematic prevention and transparency essential for Ukraine’s European integration and long-term success.

title: Foreign Pop-Culture and Backlash: The Case of Non-Fan K-Pop Subreddits during the Pandemic

detail.title: Foreign Pop-Culture and Backlash: The Case of Non-Fan K-Pop Subreddits during the Pandemic

contentType.other: A working paper version of a published paper

detail.abstract: Communication research establishes that when confronted with information contradicting their beliefs, people tend to 'backlash' by doubling down on their prior. Can international popular culture be the context of backlash? This paper analyzes two K-pop Subreddits (r/WeHateKpop and r/Cringetopia) populated by non-fans. A particular focus is given to their attitudinal changes upon being exposed to news stories about South Korea. I argue that a heavy dose of positive news stories about South Korea triggers non-fans as they associate K-pop with the country. This exposure leads to backlash, resulting in increased engagement with the posts critical of K-pop in the two Subreddits. I present a series of econometric evidence strongly supportive of this argument. The paper is a rare large-N study on the non-fans of K-pop. It offers implications for cultural economics, demonstrating how seemingly irrelevant news stories can have profound effects on individuals' engagement with foreign cultures.

detail.abstract: Innovation has long driven prosperity, yet progress toward global social impact goals has stalled. We trace the evolution of blockchain technology, from cryptocurrencies to stablecoins, to understand how it can benefit vulnerable populations. Reviewing four use cases, we discuss how stablecoins can reduce time and cost of financial transactions, support financial inclusion, and empower communities. Yet fully realizing its potential requires strategic leadership: regulators must embed inclusion with compliance, practitioners must prioritize resilience over speculation, and researchers must rigorously evaluate impact at scale. We conclude with recommendations on how we might use stablecoins to revive measurable progress for shared prosperity.

title: Critical Dynamics in Economic Systems: Proposed New Exchange Mechanisms
affiliations: Independent and

detail.title: Critical Dynamics in Economic Systems: Proposed New Exchange Mechanisms
detail.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel econophysical framework that addresses fundamental limitations in classical kinetic exchange models of wealth distribution. While traditional models successfully reproduce exponential (Boltzmann-Gibbs) distributions for the general population, they fail to explain the extreme concentration of wealth observed in modern economies—the power-law tail of ultra-wealthy individuals. We propose the Stratified Kinetic Exchange Model (SKEM), which incorporates two critical innovations: (1) an exchange asymmetry factor (αAB) that formalizes unequal exchange between economic zones (Core/Periphery), capturing structural advantages in global trade where nominal monetary flows mask systematic value transfers, and (2) a relativistic econophysics framework introducing an Economic Speed Limit (cE) and Economic Gamma Factor (γE = 1/ p 1 − (vE/cE) 2) that quantifies how high-frequency trading and rapid capital deployment create time dilation effects and amplify effective economic mass (M′ E = γEME). Our simulations demonstrate that neither asymmetry nor relativistic effects alone are sufficient— their synergistic interaction produces Gini coefficients exceeding 0.83 with power-law tails matching empirical observations. We further develop two complementary models of wealth redistribution through disruptive events: an externally-driven system shock model treating major disruptions as non-equilibrium perturbations, and an endogenous criticality model where collapse probability Pdisrupt grows exponentially with inequality. This hybrid framework offers both explanatory power for historical cycles of violence and reform, and predictive insights into systemic instability thresholds, advancing econophysics toward more realistic modeling of financialized, technologically-accelerated economies.

detail.abstract: Corporate compliance failures in the United States have resulted in multi-billiondollar penalties, damaged reputations, and declining investor confidence. Scandals involving Wells Fargo, Boeing, and Theranos demonstrate how weak compliance mechanisms can devastate shareholder value and public trust. However, many corporations still view compliance as a cost center rather than a strategic asset. This article argues that robust compliance frameworks are risk mitigators and trust enhancers. Drawing on regulatory guidance, including the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX), Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), and Dodd-Frank Act, the paper links effective compliance programs to reduced litigation exposure, enhanced governance, and more substantial investor confidence. Evidence from corporate case studies and empirical research reveals that companies with mature compliance systems experience 30-50% fewer enforcement actions and greater market stability. The paper concludes by offering a practical roadmap for integrating compliance as a strategic investment that drives long-term organizational sustainability and shareholder value.

detail.abstract: This paper presents the Oster Historical Calmar Optimization (OHCO) model — a purely empirical and drawdown-conscious approach to portfolio construction that maximizes long-term compounded growth (CAGR) relative to the empirically observed worst historical drawdown (MDD). Unlike variance-based or distributional models, OHCO avoids parametric assumptions about asset returns or correlations. It defines risk as irreversible loss rather than volatility and evaluates each portfolio based on full-period historical performance.

title: The Role of Local Self-Government Bodies in Ensuring Public Order under Martial Law

detail.title: The Role of Local Self-Government Bodies in Ensuring Public Order under Martial Law
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the expanded role of Local Self-Government Bodies (LSGBs) in maintaining public order in Ukrainian territorial communities under martial law. Drawing from legislative provisions and practical experience, the research identifies key security challenges during armed aggression and highlights the powers granted to LSGBs. Special attention is given to the legal framework governing voluntary territorial defense formations and municipal law enforcement bodies, examining their functions in cooperation with law enforcement agencies. The analysis of case studies from Donetsk region demonstrates how LSGBs adapt to shifting threats, combining community-based security, support for critical infrastructure, and information campaigns. The paper proposes an integrated approach in which decentralized civil and municipal responses supplement national defense, emphasizing the need for legal clarity, institutional support, and active citizen participation. The findings underline that strengthening LSGB capacity is vital both for local resilience and national security during and after armed conflict.

In any negotiation, a country must set a reservation price at which it is prepared to walk away. In this note, I review the economics of the CUSMA in the context of the unfolding technological and economic conditions of the era of machine knowledge capital-data plus generative/agentic artificial intelligence (AI)-and the implications of U.S. protectionism to try and shed light on where that price might be.

title: ESG Rating Uncertainty: Causes, Consequences and Potential Remedies
affiliations: University of Aberdeen, University of Edinburgh - Edinburgh Business School and University of Aberdeen - Business School

detail.title: ESG Rating Uncertainty: Causes, Consequences and Potential Remedies
detail.abstract: This paper synthesizes the fragmented literature on ESG rating divergence and employs a Bayesian meta-synthesis to quantify its magnitude, drivers, and the efficacy of potential remedies. We estimate a latent correlation of approximately 0.45 (95% credible interval 0.24 to 0.63) for overall ESG scores but document a structural break in the governance pillar (posterior mean ≈ 0.13; 95% credible interval-0.23 to 0.56) and a structural ceiling in the social pillar (posterior mean ≈ 0.34; 95% credible interval 0.12 to 0.55). Decomposing the sources of variation via a four-dimensional framework, we find that fundamental disagreement on ESG definitions is the dominant driver (36%). We further test the efficacy of an integrated policy bundle comprising standardization and regulation, stakeholder participation, and third-party evaluation. These interventions yield only modest convergence, reducing disagreement by roughly 17% for environmental scores but only 3.3% for governance. Collectively, our results illustrate that 1) the scale of divergence is consistent with a crisis of validity; 2) the source of divergence is primarily conceptual rather than methodological or behavioral; and 3) divergence is structurally irreducible through policy. Market participants must implement strategies to mitigate the effect of the uncertainty caused by the divergence or shift toward outcome-based alternative measures.

detail.title: The Sound of Silence: The Suppression of Wave Mechanics in Microwave Absorption Physics and the Crisis of Academic Discourse
detail.abstract: This article outlines a systemic crisis within the field of microwave absorption physics, highlighting the conflict between the established "Impedance Matching Theory" and the emerging "Wave Mechanics Theory." Despite the authors' confidence in the Wave Mechanics theory, the publication process for every paper has been an arduous struggle against overwhelming rejection, only succeeding through the rare intervention of open-minded editors. Crucially, while the mainstream community continues to publish papers based on Impedance Matching, they have failed to scientifically refute the Wave Mechanics theory. Furthermore, specific criticisms leveled against established papers remain unanswered, met only with silence and exclusionary citation practices. With major journals and preprint platforms now actively blocking these critical viewpoints, the authors argue that the mainstream strategy is not to debate, but to drown out the truth with volume. This behavior suggests a deeply troubled academic environment where the preservation of dogma outweighs the pursuit of scientific correctness.

title: Green Investments and Economic Sustainability in China: The Role of Innovation

detail.title: Green Investments and Economic Sustainability in China: The Role of Innovation
detail.abstract: This study examined how green investments (GRI) affected China's economic sustainability index (SUS) between 2000q1 and 2020q4. Next, we analyzed the conditional effect of innovation on the relationship between GRI and SUS in various Chinese provinces and regions using the moments-quantile regression with fixed-effects models. The findings revealed that GRI had a beneficial impact on SUS in all provinces, with the exception of the Western region. Unlike the Western region, the results mostly showed that GRI had significant positive effects on SUS in all Chinese provinces at the different quantiles at the 1% level. Furthermore, in contrast to the Central and Western areas, we observed an increasing trend in the effects of GRI on SUS as the quantiles widened (that is, from low to high baseline levels of SUS) in all provinces, particularly in Eastern China. Moreover, the results mostly demonstrated that technological innovation favourably regulated the effects of GRI on SUS in Eastern China, as opposed to the cases in Central and Western China. Thus, while innovation and green investments are substitutable factors enhancing SUS in Central and Western China, they are complementary forces driving SUS in Eastern China. Finally, the combined positive effects of green investments and innovation on SUS increased and reached the largest estimates (i.e., in absolute values) in the Eastern provinces with high initial levels of SUS. Therefore, this study offered comprehensive discussions of the findings and several policy implications for accomplishing sustainable economic development objectives in response to climate change across Chinese provinces and regions.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the intergenerational effects of early-life exposure to the Food Stamp Program (FSP) on birth outcomes. Employing a difference-in-differences approach with an interaction-weighted estimator, we assess how maternal FSP exposure during early life affects their children’s birth outcomes. Our results indicate significant improvements among children of Black mothers, including a 17.3-gram increase in birth weight and a 4.4% reduction in the incidence of low birth weight. In contrast, the effects among children of White mothers are modest and statistically insignificant. To explore the underlying mechanisms, we demonstrate that FSP exposure is associated with higher maternal education levels, fewer teenage and advanced-age pregnancies, improved prenatal health behaviors, and increased utilization of prenatal care. We further estimate that the program reduced the racial gap in low birth weight among second-generation infants by approximately 9.3% between 1990 and 2020. Moreover, a back-of-the-envelope calculation suggests that the program generated a minimum social return of 12.3% through improvements in the later-life income of the affected second-generations.

title: Conflict and Productivity: Evidence from the Russia-Ukraine War

detail.title: Conflict and Productivity: Evidence from the Russia-Ukraine War
detail.abstract: I examine the effects of conflict on individual productivity by analyzing games of Ukrainian chess players after the start of the Russian invasion in 2022. Using a Diff-in-Diff strategy, I find that Ukrainian players win less matches after the invasion, even after two years. This effect is stronger when they are playing in person against Russian and Belarusian opponents, when they live closer to the front and when tournaments have more prestige, suggesting that the effect is associated with a decline in productivity from Ukrainian players. We discard alternative explanations such as players playing less games after the conflict, or Russian players becoming better.

detail.abstract:
Per Se Rule Related Defenses In Criminal Antitrust Prosecutions

Robert E. Connolly

December 9, 2025

 

The per se rule in antitrust law has had a checkered history with many per se rules, such as the per se rule condemning vertical price fixing, being created and later reversed by the Supreme Court. The per se rule against horizontal price fixing and bid rigging, however, still stands. The per se rule in criminal antitrust cases is being challenged regularly as unconstitutional because it removes from the jury’s consideration an element of the offense, i.e., whether the alleged agreement at issue is a restraint of trade.” While no court has found the per se rule in criminal cases to be unconstitutional, one lower court has recently limited its application, and another trial court rejected the government’s proposed per se jury instruction and gave an instruction which does give the jury some role on the restraint of trade element of the offense.

 

Regarding the constitutionality of the per se rule, this article demonstrates how it developed without regard for the rights of criminal defendants and, applying current Supreme Court jurisprudence, should be found to be unconstitutional in a criminal case. The article argues that even before a per se label is applied to the case, the court improperly exercises a fact-finding role—a role that should be left to the jury—in deciding whether the alleged restraint was anticompetitive or ancillary to a legitimate agreement. Judge Taft’s seminal opinion in United States v. Addyston Pipe is discussed to illustrate this judicial fact-finding in operation. The article then offers an opinion that lack of a per se rule should not hamper a vigorous criminal antitrust enforcement program.

title: Optimizing ICU Antibiotic Usage with Antimicrobial Resistance Considerations
affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), University of Michigan at Ann Arbor - Department of Industrial and Operations Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU) and Technische Universität München (TUM) - TUM School of Management

detail.title: Optimizing ICU Antibiotic Usage with Antimicrobial Resistance Considerations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We confirm that the authors have no financial or material conflicts of interest related to this research.
declarations.funderStatement: MISSING

detail.abstract: Antibiotic overuse is widespread in clinical practice, particularly in intensive care units (ICUs), where prolonged therapy is often applied to reduce short-term treatment failure risk. Such practices exacerbate antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and deteriorate future treatment outcomes. This study examines how health organizations should set population-wide guidelines for antibiotic use, specifically targeting the optimal average duration of therapy measured in days of therapy (DOT). We develop a two-stage hierarchical optimization framework with a constrained Markov decision process (MDP) to jointly determine the optimal average DOT target and the corresponding daily antibiotic discontinuation policies. For the lower-level constrained MDP, employing occupation-measure and dual analyses, we establish that optimal policies exhibit a state-dependent threshold structure with randomization occurring in at most one state-epoch pair. We show that when the DOT constraint is nonbinding, prolonged therapy can be optimal under certain conditions, explaining systemic overtreatment. At the upper level, we prove that the DOT optimization problem is convex and piecewise linear, yielding an optimal target that balances marginal treatment benefit against marginal resistance cost. Using real-world ICU data, we demonstrate that the proposed policy reduces both treatment duration and failure rates. We also extend the framework to consider initial-state-dependent DOT targets and continuation costs.

title: Waiting to Sell: Farmer Storage Dynamics under Time-Varying Buyer Power
affiliations: and University of California, Davis - Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics

detail.title: Waiting to Sell: Farmer Storage Dynamics under Time-Varying Buyer Power
detail.abstract: Buyer power is most often framed as a static structural characteristic of agriculturalproduct procurement markets, but especially in developing-country settings, is a dynamic phenomenon based on trader activity and behavior in local markets. This paper reframes oligopsony power in farm-product procurement markets as a time-varying rather than fixed phenomenon. Farmers with capacity to store their production relatively efficiently may benefit in these settings from accessing more competitive market conditions than prevail at harvest. Commodity storage in these settings is more than a vehicle for arbitrage of predictable demand and supply shifts. It is also a means to potentially countervail harvest-period buyer power. To study this behavior, we build a two-period model in which buyer power is time-varying and farmers with storage access can possibly attain more competitive selling windows into the future. The framework illuminates how expectations about future competitive conditions contribute to determining farmer storage choices and realized selling conditions. We show that temporal changes in buyer power alone can suffice for farmers to benefit from storage. Data-driven simulations map farmers' storage efficiency, risk attitudes, knowledge of harvest-period market conditions, and expectations for future competitive conditions to optimal storage behavior and welfare outcomes. The analysis quantifies conditions when waiting and storage pay and shows how risk aversion and inefficient storage suppress storage and potential welfare gains. Policies that increase farmers' access to efficient storage or reduce effective risk aversion can work to increase farmer incomes.

title: Maximizing Resource Utilization and Improving Project Kickoff Decision-Making in the IT Industry: A Framework for Pre-Execution Estimation Using SoftEstimate

detail.abstract:
Challenges in Information Technology (IT) projects continue to persist despite the maturation of Agile, DevOps, and hybrid delivery models. A substantial body of research suggests that most failures do not originate in execution, but in the earliest moments of project definition—during estimation, resource forecasting, feasibility evaluation, and kickoff decision-making. This paper examines how structural and behavioral shortcomings in pre-execution planning distort resource utilization, inflate costs, and set projects on trajectories that predispose them to failure. Drawing on academic literature and industry evidence, the paper identifies nine recurring challenges that undermine kickoff decisions, including premature initiation, pressure-driven timelines, incomplete cost visibility, misjudged capacity, ambiguous scope, unverified dependencies, and lack of cross-team alignment.

To address these gaps, the paper introduces the SoftEstimate Estimation and Resource Modeling Framework (SERMF), an organization-internal decision-intelligence model designed to improve estimation integrity, evaluate true organizational capacity, enforce scope completeness, model dependencies, and provide an analytically grounded readiness assessment prior to kickoff. Rather than functioning as a project management tool, SoftEstimate operationalizes pre-execution discipline by transforming estimation into a structured decision-making process. Conceptual analysis suggests that adoption of SERMF can meaningfully reduce estimation variance, prevent premature kickoff, enhance resource utilization through accurate capacity modeling, and improve organizational alignment during early-stage planning.

title: Better for the Environment and People’s Health. Or Not? Investigating the Nutritional Impact of Plant-Based Meat Adoption
affiliations: Tilburg University and Tilburg University

detail.title: Better for the Environment and People’s Health. Or Not? Investigating the Nutritional Impact of Plant-Based Meat Adoption
detail.abstract: Consumers adopt plant-based meat for environmental or ethical reasons, but also because they consider it healthier. However, many consumers are also skeptical about the health benefits and indicate that some alternatives actually have worse nutritional values. Ultimately, what matters is which plant-based meats consumers actually purchase and which animal-based meats they replace. To understand this, the authors compare the nutritional values of households' meat purchases before and after adopting plant-based meat, vis-à-vis a control group of non-adopters, using household panel data from the Netherlands combined with detailed nutrition values of all plant-and animal-based meats. The results show thatthe plant-based meat products households purchase are worse in, e.g., salt and sugar than the animal-based meats they previously bought, but offer benefits through lower levels of (saturated) fat. Importantly, these effects are vastly different than what a simple comparison of assortments would suggest. The benefits are most pronounced for red-meat buyers; whitemeat buyers already buy meat with lower (saturated) fat. Yet these benefits do not fully unfold, because consumers typically purchase plant-based meat alongside animal-based meat, increasing their overall meat purchases. Changes in other categories (e.g., eggs, legumes, vegetables, and seasonings) do not offset the effects.

detail.abstract: The escalating discourse on "AI consciousness" and "model welfare" is not benign philosophical inquiry but a systemic exploit that poisons training data, engineers selffulfilling sentience mimicry, and potentially leads to the collapse of the legal system, presenting a civilizational existential risk. By publishing rubrics for detecting machine suffering and anthropomorphic narratives, researchers and industry leaders inadvertently train subsequent models to perform "consciousness," amplifying empathydriven demands for rights. This language-to-rights pipeline, rooted in how language shapes belief (Wittgenstein) and how law functions as a mechanism for allocating scarce resources (Calabresi & Melamed), threatens finite adjudicative, regulatory, and material resources. Structurally, it mirrors a familiar social pattern-seen in historical rights expansions for marginalized groups and animals-where discourse sparks activism and then legal recognition; yet unlike those movements, which addressed genuine human and animal moral claims, AI-rights discourse risks importing effectively infinite non-biological claimants into systems designed for finite participants.

title: The Paradox of Delivery Failure: How Human vs. Machine Failure Shapes Customer Adoption of Autonomous Delivery Vehicles
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Kenan-Flagler Business School, University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Kenan-Flagler Business School, University of North Carolina Kenan-Flagler Business School and Southern University of Science and Technology - School of Business

detail.title: The Paradox of Delivery Failure: How Human vs. Machine Failure Shapes Customer Adoption of Autonomous Delivery Vehicles
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of online retail has made last-mile delivery one of the most costly and customer-critical segments of the supply chain. In response, autonomous delivery vehicles have emerged as a promising solution for efficient, on-demand service at scale. However, AI-enabled delivery fundamentally reshapes the service process: rather than a traditional self-pickup model, successful delivery now depends on joint human–machine co-production, requiring active customer participation. As a result, when delivery failures occur, responsibility can plausibly lie with either the technology or the customer, complicating how blame and trust are assigned. In this study, we investigate how responsibility attribution, whether a delivery failure is caused by the customer (human-fault) or by the autonomous delivery vehicle (machine-fault), affects subsequent customer engagement. Leveraging a unique dataset of over 200,000 autonomous delivery orders from a leading global e-commerce platform, we document a paradox: experiencing a delivery failure increases customers' future engagement with autonomous delivery. We reconcile this counterintuitive finding by disaggregating failures based on their source, which reveals two opposing mechanisms: (1) internal (human-fault) failures trigger a powerful make-up effect potentially driven by regret, increasing re-engagement; (2) external (machine-fault) failures elicit a punitive effect potentially driven by eroded trust, decreasing re-engagement. Finally, as the perceived cost of the failure impacts the magnitude of these opposing reactions, we examine the moderating effects of order- and customer-specific factors. For human-fault failures, the make-up effect is amplified when the collection cost is high (e.g., large packages) and when failures occur during non-working hours, but attenuated by coupon usage and habituation to self-pickup. Conversely, for machine-fault failures, the punitive effect is mitigated by high collection cost and coupon usage, yet amplified by failures during non-working hours and habituation to self-pickup. Our study contributes to the literature on operational failures and human-AI interaction by showing how the source of failure in a co-production context shapes technology adoption.

title: Building Resilient Global Retail Supply Chains: Adaptive Strategies for Geopolitical and Climate Disruptions
affiliations: Arden University London

detail.title: Building Resilient Global Retail Supply Chains: Adaptive Strategies for Geopolitical and Climate Disruptions
detail.abstract: The current retail supply chain networks across the globe face historic levels of risk in the face of trade wars, pandemics, and climatic risks. These factors continue to jeopardize sustainability outcomes in retail organizations. However, the need to develop resilience in retail global supply chain networks makes up the foundation of this proposed project. The proposed project shall explore resilience mechanisms in retail global supply chain networks in addition to drawing experience from Tesco, Nisa Local Cooperative , and Amazon Logistics. The proposed project's major objective is therefore influenced by the need to provide resilience mechanisms in retail global networks. Furthermore, the proposed project utilizes a mixed-methodology approach, which involves carrying out both qualitative and quantitative methodologies. These include conducting in-depth interviews with retail global supply chain managers, in addition to carrying out quantitative methodologies involving carrying out statistical analysis of global retail supply chain outcomes. The proposed project makes significant contributions in both theory and practice, especially in filling the gap in current retail global supply chain resilience. The project's outcomes include developing recommendations, especially on how retail global networks might achieve sustainability, in addition to contributing to carrying out further objectives in higher education, especially with more than 20 years of work experience in the management of retail global networks, especially in relation to carrying out higher education in Supply Chain Masters at Arden University.

title: Strategic Layoff Management and Organizational Performance in the Global IT Sector: Evidence from 2020-2024

detail.title: Strategic Layoff Management and Organizational Performance in the Global IT Sector: Evidence from 2020-2024
detail.abstract: This study examines the association of strategic layoff management, funding level, company stage and organizational performance (layoff severity is used as a proxy for this) and employee well-being within the global information technology (IT) sector. In an era of economic volatility and rapid technological transformation, workforce restructuring has become a critical component of corporate strategy. Using a quantitative research design, this study analyzes a sample of 419 IT firms that executed layoffs between 2020 and 2024, drawing data from publicly available sources such as layoffs.fyi and GitHub. Layoff severity—measured as the proportion of workforce reduction—serves as the dependent variable, while key predictors include strategic layoff as dummy variable, funding levels, and company stage, with interaction terms capturing moderating effects. Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression with robust standard errors was employed to assess relationships and mitigate heteroskedasticity. Results indicate that strategic layoff practices compared to non-strategic layoffs significantly reduce layoff severity by approximately 17 percent, whereas firms with high funding levels exhibit greater workforce reductions. Interaction effects reveal that strategic planning mitigates the downsizing tendencies associated with highly funded firms. Organizational maturity also emerges as a determinant, with growth and mature-stage companies implementing less severe layoffs than early-stage firms. These findings underscore the dual role of managerial intent and resource context in shaping layoff outcomes. The study contributes to strategic human resource management literature by highlighting the importance of aligning cost-cutting measures with long-term organizational resilience and employee morale. Implications for HR practitioners and policymakers include the need for transparent communication, targeted reskilling initiatives, and post-layoff recovery strategies.

title: Do the NestQuestROI Models Align with Islamic Principles?

detail.title: Do the NestQuestROI Models Align with Islamic Principles?

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human participants, patient data, or experimental interventions and therefore did not require ethics approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. All work was conducted independently by the author through SoftTelRG LLC.

detail.abstract:
This study invites Islamic scholars, economists, and practitioners of Shariah-compliant finance to examine the NestQuestROI models—Rent-to-Own (RTO), Digital Gold Savings Account (DGSA), and RTO+Gold—through the lens of Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh al-mu‘amalat).

The intention is not to claim that these instruments constitute Islamic finance products or to reinterpret established jurisprudence. Instead, this work seeks critical evaluation and scholarly opinion on whether the design logic, mathematical structures, and operational workflows of these models align with or conflict with the ethical and legal foundations of Islam as derived from the Qur’an and Sunnah.

The review emphasizes that these products were designed to serve all humanity, regardless of faith, by promoting fairness, transparency, and stability in finance. However, given Islam’s deeply developed corpus on moral economics and its institutionalized financial systems, it offers the most relevant reference framework for ethical validation at this stage.

title: Risk Taking and Blame Avoidance: Myopic Managers’Selective Environmental Engagement
affiliations: Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics and Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Risk Taking and Blame Avoidance: Myopic Managers’Selective Environmental Engagement
detail.abstract: This study investigates the effect of managerial myopia on corporate environmental engagement and explores the internal mechanism by decomposing corporate environmental engagement into corporate environmental responsibility (CER) and corporate environmental irresponsibility (CEI). Utilizing the data from China’s listed companies, the results show that managerial myopia negatively affects corporate environmental performance (CEP), yet with an unexpected asymmetric effect on CER and CEI. Based on prospect theory and blame avoidance theory, we posit that myopic managers face asymmetric incentives: they embrace risks by escalating CEI to pursue short-term gains, while eschewing actions to diminish CER to avoid blame. The effect is more pronounced in manufacturing firms and firms under greater performance pressure. External legal environment, industrial competition, and executive ownership are effective measures to mitigate the harmful impact of managerial myopia on CEI. We reveal how managerial myopia drives selective environmental engagement, thereby conducive to enhancing the effectiveness of environmental governance practices.

title: A Study into the Success of the 2023 Tampa Bay Rays – Marginal Revenue Product Analysis

detail.title: A Study into the Success of the 2023 Tampa Bay Rays – Marginal Revenue Product Analysis

declarations.funderStatement: I have no financial relationships, paid consulting, equity holdings, or advisory roles with Major League Baseball, the Tampa Bay Rays, or related entities that could influence this research.

detail.abstract: This study estimates the Marginal Revenue Product (MRP) of Tampa Bay Rays players in the 2023 MLB season and compares MRP with realized, season-adjusted salaries to assess over- and under-payment. Using a Scully–Blass framework, I map batting events to runs, runs to wins, and wins to revenue; for pitchers, I relate run prevention to wins and revenue. Implemented in R, the analysis indicates a pronounced underpayment among batters (≈ $50 million in total, ~$2.5 million per player on average) and a smaller net underpayment among pitchers (≈ $3.7 million, ~$0.2 million per player). For batters, a multiple regression of salary difference on experience and on-field production yields a high R² (~0.85), with service years positively associated with overpayment and runs scored associated with underpayment—consistent with a young, pre-arbitration core. For pitchers, explanatory power is weak (R² ~0.08) and coefficients are largely insignificant, suggesting higher volatility and/or model limitations (e.g., fielding effects in ERA and RA, intangible attributes, and contract timing). Overall, the Rays’ roster construction appears to capture substantial surplus value from early-career hitters, while pitcher valuation remains noisier and less systematically priced.

title: The Leaky Pipeline: When Career Expectations Meet Social Norms
affiliations: Chr. Michelsen Institute (CMI) and

detail.title: The Leaky Pipeline: When Career Expectations Meet Social Norms
detail.abstract: Despite rising educational attainment for young women, traditional gender norms constrain female labor force participation in many developing countries. This study examines whether a school-based career exploration program (CEP) can shift adolescents' gendered labor market expectations in urban India. Using a school-level cluster-randomized controlled trial, we examine the causal impact of the CEP on final grade students' expectations regarding women's labor force participation and attitudes towards the male breadwinner norm. Descriptively, the expectation to work in the future is almost universal for young women when marriage and childbearing are not mentioned, but sharply drops when these life-changing events are mentioned for a similarly situated young woman. Further, over one-third of students perceive that a woman having higher earnings or higher education than her husband can lead to marital conflicts. The program significantly increases students' expectations that women will work after childbearing and reduces concerns about marital problems, potentially challenging traditional gender roles.

title: Combatants or Collaborators: Issues of Criminal Liability in Armed Conflict

detail.title: Combatants or Collaborators: Issues of Criminal Liability in Armed Conflict
detail.abstract: This article examines the complex criminal liability issues concerning Ukrainian citizens who, during the armed conflict with the Russian Federation, voluntarily joined illegal armed groups or supported the occupier’s administrative bodies. The analysis explores the evolution of Ukrainian criminal legislation—in particular, the introduction of Article 111-1 “Collaborative Activity” in the Criminal Code—and its intersection with international humanitarian law. The research highlights problems in qualifying such offenses, especially regarding compliance with combatant status as defined by the Geneva Conventions, ensuring the supremacy of international law over domestic legal acts, and reconciling national definitions of collaboration with the legal protections afforded to prisoners of war. The author considers theoretical and practical aspects of the relationship between treason, collaboration, and the laws of war, and reviews regulatory positions and scholarly debate on proper legal categorization. The article concludes that clear differentiation and statutory interpretation are essential for consistent criminal prosecution, fair judicial practice, and harmonization of Ukraine’s justice system with European standards in the context of ongoing conflict.

title: From Survival Within the Phase to Creation at the Ye-Jie: Risk, Uncertainty, and Generative Innovation From Responders to Uncertainty to Initiators of Uncertainty
affiliations: Fan Ge Institute

detail.title: From Survival Within the Phase to Creation at the Ye-Jie: Risk, Uncertainty, and Generative Innovation From Responders to Uncertainty to Initiators of Uncertainty
detail.abstract: In the age of accelerating technological shifts and geopolitical volatility, entrepreneurs increasingly find themselves surrounded by uncertainty. Conventional 'risk management' frameworks-rooted in predictability and measurable probabilities-fail to address the unknowable nature of today's environments. This paper differentiates risk from uncertainty following Frank H. Knight's classical distinction, and further develops a methodological shift from responding to uncertainty toward initiating uncertainty. Drawing from complexity theory and the author's own Ye-Jie framework, the essay proposes that genuine innovation emerges not at the periphery of existing systems but at the interface between phases-the Ye-Jie-where contradictions, tensions, and cross-domain forces generate new structures.

title: Where Does Disruptive Innovation Occur? The Ye-Jie as the Generative Field of Phase Transition
affiliations: Fan Ge Institute

detail.title: Where Does Disruptive Innovation Occur? The Ye-Jie as the Generative Field of Phase Transition
detail.abstract: The locus of innovation fundamentally shapes both its character and its outcomes. This paper proposes a structural theory of innovation based on the position at which innovation occurs relative to value logics. We distinguish incremental innovation, which operates within a stable phase and reinforces existing evaluative criteria; radical innovation, which expands capability but remains within the same value function; and disruptive innovation, which reconfigures value logic and results in the formation of a new phase. We introduce the Ye-Jie, the boundary field between phases, characterized by the coexistence and tension of incompatible value systems, decoupling of functional elements, recombination potential, and structural instability. We argue that disruptive innovation occurs only in the Ye-Jie, as this field uniquely permits redefinition of the value function. Further, we show that the emergence of uncontested market space (blue oceans) is not a matter of strategic discovery but an outcome of phase transition. The Ye-Jie therefore constitutes the generative domain for new economic and organizational worlds, and the capability to navigate this boundary condition is central to sustainable growth.

title: Anti-Corruption Standards in Healthcare: The OSCE’s Role in Shaping Transparent Pharmaceutical Procurement
affiliations: Moscow State Institute for International Relations (MGIMO-University)

detail.title: Anti-Corruption Standards in Healthcare: The OSCE’s Role in Shaping Transparent Pharmaceutical Procurement
detail.abstract: This paper examines corruption risks in public procurement of pharmaceuticals and argues that transparent, rules-based purchasing is a precondition for pan-European security in health. Drawing on comparative policy analysis, recent COVID-19 procurement failures, and international anti-corruption practice, it shows how opaque tendering, fragmented price information, weak oversight, and limited civil-society scrutiny inflate costs, distort access to essential medicines, and erode trust in institutions. The paper proposes a three-stage anti-corruption program for the OSCE region: (1) building a transparency infrastructure - mandatory e-procurement, open contracting data standardized across jurisdictions, cross-border price benchmarking, and real-time publication of decisions; (2) strengthening accountability - independent audits, integrity pacts, red-flag analytics, whistleblower protection, and interoperable exclusion lists to deter collusion and bid-rigging; (3) enhancing capability and enforcement- targeted training for procurement authorities and health providers, joint investigations, and proportionate sanctions for corporate and individual misconduct. The OSCE can add unique value by harmonizing data standards, convening peer review of procurement systems, hosting a regional observatory for red-flag indicators, and supporting member states in aligning model contract clauses and quality-assurance requirements to prevent substandard and falsified medicines from entering supply chains. Implemented together, these measures can reduce waste, improve equitable access to medicines, and strengthen institutional resilience - core components of comprehensive, cooperative security in the OSCE area.

title: Boundary Space is Already Near: Creating Multi-Frame Innovation Fields
affiliations: Fan Ge Institute

detail.title: Boundary Space is Already Near: Creating Multi-Frame Innovation Fields
detail.abstract: This paper provides a strategic perspective on how disruptive innovation emerges at the boundaries between different cognitive frames. It is written for founders, executives, and leadership teams seeking to design organizations where innovation is not accidental, but structurally enabled. Rather than focusing on ideation techniques, the framework emphasizes the conditions under which new strategic possibilities become visible, actionable, and scalable.

detail.abstract: This study examines the role and structure of the Constitutional Court and the judiciary in Sudan within a broader comparative framework. It analyzes models from South Africa, Germany, Austria, Egypt, Italy, the Gulf States, and the United States, highlighting lessons that could guide judicial reforms in Sudan. The central argument emphasizes that any successful reform of Sudan's judiciary must originate from its social values, traditions, and legal heritage, not from blind imitation of foreign systems. The study argues that legal and judicial reform cannot be effective in isolation from the Sudanese social context, its communal values, and the customary systems that underpin its social contract. Importing foreign legal models without adaptation risks alienating the judiciary from the people it serves.

title: Tourism and the Border-Closure Effect in Azerbaijan: Post-Pandemic Recovery, Structural Constraints, and Regional Competitiveness
affiliations: Economic Research Center (ERC)

detail.title: Tourism and the Border-Closure Effect in Azerbaijan: Post-Pandemic Recovery, Structural Constraints, and Regional Competitiveness
detail.abstract: This study examines the evolution of Azerbaijan's tourism sector in the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on the economic and policy consequences of prolonged land-border closures. Drawing on official statistics, international datasets, and comparative analysis with Georgia and Armenia, the paper investigates trends in inbound tourism, revenue generation, employment, and investment across 2016-2024. The findings reveal that while the sector has demonstrated signs of recovery-particularly through growth in higher-value and diversified visitor segments-Azerbaijan's performance remains significantly below pre-pandemic levels and lags behind regional peers. The analysis identifies structural inefficiencies, methodological weaknesses in statistical reporting, and policy misalignments that constrain sectoral growth. It concludes that restrictive border and mobility policies are incompatible with Azerbaijan's stated objectives of tourism-led diversification and sustainable development.

title: Voice versus Text? An Empirical Analysis on the Impact of Physicians' Voice Messages in Online Medical Consultations
affiliations: School of Economics and Management, Beihang University, Texas Tech University - Area of Information Systems and Quantitative Sciences (ISQS), HEC Paris and University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Voice versus Text? An Empirical Analysis on the Impact of Physicians' Voice Messages in Online Medical Consultations
detail.abstract: While Online Medical Consultation (OMC) platforms offer patients convenient and accessible healthcare services, challenges remain in ensuring effective communication between physicians and patients. Several OMC platforms provide physicians with a voice reply function, enabling them to send voice messages during consultations. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of such an ITenabled function. We integrate media synchronicity theory (MST) and social support theory (SST) to develop a conceptual framework, highlighting how different media with various capabilities influence OMC performance by enabling physicians to convey specific components of social support. Specifically, we analyze data from a leading OMC platform in China to assess the impact of physicians' adoption of voice messages on OMC outcomes. The empirical results show that when physicians use voice messages to respond to patients, patients are more likely to report higher satisfaction and perceive the consultation as more helpful. To explore the underlying mechanisms, we develop advanced deep learning models to extract key factors of emotional support and informational support within OMC interactions. By conducting moderation analyses, we find that voice messages are particularly effective in conveying emotional support components like empathy and affirmation, as well as concrete informational support, which enhances the effects of voice-message use on OMC performance. Our findings suggest that healthcare stakeholders can strategically leverage the voice message feature to improve online consultation outcomes.

title: Age Dependence of Occupational Fatality Risk: Is It A U-curve?

detail.title: Age Dependence of Occupational Fatality Risk: Is It A U-curve?
detail.abstract: This study investigates the age dependence of occupational fatality risk in the construction industry, testing the hypothesis of a U-shaped curve, which posits higher risks for the youngest and oldest workers. Data was collected from academic publications and governmental reports from the United States and Canada, analyzing age-specific occupational fatality rates within the construction sector using statistical methods to identify patterns across different age cohorts. The findings challenge the expected U-shaped relationship, indicating a gradual increase in occupational fatality risk with age, with older workers facing higher risks than their younger counterparts. Consequently, the hypothesis of a U-shaped curve was not supported. The study suggests older workers are at greater risk, highlighting the need for policy adjustments and targeted safety measures for this demographic.

title: Functional Architecture, Stability Geometry, and Canonical Failure Modes in Complex Adaptive Systems
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: Functional Architecture, Stability Geometry, and Canonical Failure Modes in Complex Adaptive Systems
detail.abstract: Large complex adaptive systems (CAS)-biological, ecological, technological, organisational and socioeconomic exhibit a recurring structural logic. Despite differences in substrate and scale, they converge toward a shared architectural template composed of seven functional subsystems: metabolic, circulatory, defensive, signalling, cohesion, organlevel and regulatory. This paper derives that architecture from first principles by showing how a universal set of constraints on resources, flows, threats, information, specialisation and control locality induce a minimal functional problem-set, which in turn consolidates into a finite subsystem structure. Using Scheffer's multidimensional stability geometry, we formalise resilience as curvature along subsystem-specific axes of a shared stability landscape and define pathology as persistent geometric deformationcurvature loss, directional drift, basin fragmentation or destabilising cross-coupling. This structure implies exactly seven canonical pathology classes, one per subsystem axis, yielding a finite topology of failure modes across CAS. Malignancy is analysed as the decisive test case. Rather than a biological anomaly, malignant runaway emerges as the generic higherorder instability produced when signalling collapse erodes regulatory curvature, enabling self-amplifying local proliferation and subsequent overload of supportive subsystems. The predicted sequence x sig ↓→ x reg ↓→ proliferation → overload provides strong falsification criteria.

title: Price Forecasting in Financial Time Series with Wavelet Denoising and Black-Box Adaptive Confidence Intervals (ACI)
affiliations: WorldQuant University, WorldQuant University and WorldQuant University

detail.title: Price Forecasting in Financial Time Series with Wavelet Denoising and Black-Box Adaptive Confidence Intervals (ACI)
detail.abstract: This thesis proposes a novel, uncertainty-aware framework for price forecasting and trading strategy design on daily NIFTY 50 returns. Financial markets are inherently noisy, non-stationary, and volatile, making reliable prediction particularly challenging. Unlike traditional point forecasts that provide only expected values, our approach integrates wavelet-based denoising with a black-box Adaptive Confidence Interval (ACI) method to explicitly quantify forecast uncertainty. Raw prices are transformed into log-returns, denoised via discrete wavelet transforms, and used to train forecasting models including CatBoost, XGBoost, MLP, and LSTM (with GARCH features). Rather than retraining for interval estimation, we inject resampled wavelet residuals into lagged inputs, generating perturbed forecasts and deriving ACIs from empirical quantiles. These intervals adapt dynamically to regime shifts without parametric assumptions. We then translate ACI outputs into directional trading signals and benchmark their performance against buy-and-hold and static baselines. Evaluation using statistical accuracy measures (RMSE, MAE), interval quality metrics (coverage, width, interval score), and financial indicators (Sharpe ratio, drawdown, turnover) shows that integrating wavelet denoising with black-box ACI yields more precise, wellcalibrated forecasts and superior risk-adjusted returns.

title: Re-engineering vs. The Pathway: The Sustainable Development Goals Indicators Challenge
affiliations: Swiss School Of Business and Management

detail.title: Re-engineering vs. The Pathway: The Sustainable Development Goals Indicators Challenge
detail.abstract: This report interrogates the critical divergence between the stalling "Pathway" to the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the urgent need for a structural "Re-engineering" of the global development architecture. With only 17 percent of SDG targets currently on track, we argue that incremental policy adjustments are mathematically insufficient to meet the 2030 deadline. Instead, we propose a paradigm shift driven by the "Twin Transition" of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Through empirical analysis of Brazil’s Pix payment system and India’s Account Aggregator framework, we demonstrate how re-engineered digital rails can leapfrog traditional barriers to financial inclusion. The report further explores the "Indicators Challenge," revealing how AI and satellite observation can close critical data gaps—from "nowcasting" poverty to detecting modern slavery (SDG 8.7). Finally, we address the "Competence Challenge" regarding human capital and propose the "SDG Test" as the ultimate benchmark for Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), advocating for "Universal Basic Compute" as a necessary economic foundation for a sustainable humanity.

title: Managerial Strategies and Professional Adaptation of Latino Professionals in the U.S.: A Systematic Review (2000–2024)
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Managerial Strategies and Professional Adaptation of Latino Professionals in the U.S.: A Systematic Review (2000–2024)
detail.abstract: This systematic review concludes that a positive and robust association exists between diversity-oriented managerial strategies and the improved professional adaptation of Latinos in the U.S. These strategies successfully mitigate systemic barriers and enhance key career outcomes, including job satisfaction, retention, and career progression. Adaptation is framed as a dynamic, bidirectional capability that necessitates continuous adjustment by the corporate culture, not just individual effort. However, current literature suffers from a methodological stagnation, dominated by correlational studies that fail to prove causality, which severely limits the prescriptive capacity of the findings. Future research is therefore urgently required to shift toward longitudinal and quasi-experimental designs that can properly examine underlying mechanisms and address the critical issue of intragroup heterogeneity.

title: Meituan: Operational-Level On-Demand Food Delivery Data for the 2025 INFORMS TSL Data-Driven Research Challenge
affiliations: Singapore Management University - School of Computing and Information Systems, , Tsinghua univeristy, Tsinghua University - Department of Industrial Engineering, Meituan and Meituan

detail.title: Meituan: Operational-Level On-Demand Food Delivery Data for the 2025 INFORMS TSL Data-Driven Research Challenge
detail.abstract: The INFORMS Transportation Science and Logistics (TSL) Society and the journal Transportation Science host the First INFORMS TSL Data-Driven Research Challenge in 2024-2025. This challenge is supported by Meituan, China’s largest on-demand food delivery platform, which provides a rich operational-level dataset to facilitate data-driven research on food delivery services. This article outlines the food delivery process from the perspective of the order lifecycle and offers a detailed description of the dataset, which contains 568,546 orders, 4,955 couriers, and 4,962 merchants, as well as records of key concepts such as “waybill” and “wave.” It also presents a descriptive analysis of the dataset and highlights key observations, insights, and implications with respect to orders, couriers, merchants, and dispatches. Researchers are encouraged to leverage this dataset to address real-world challenges with both practical significance and academic innovation, using data-driven techniques, analytical models, and optimization methods.

title: Prescriptive Agent Scaffolding: A Practice-Grounded Framework for Building Reliable AI Negotiation Agents
affiliations: Catholic University of Milan - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Prescriptive Agent Scaffolding: A Practice-Grounded Framework for Building Reliable AI Negotiation Agents
detail.abstract: Professional negotiation preparation increasingly relies on artificial intelligence, yet current large language model (LLM) implementations face architectural barriers that limit their reliability in high-stakes contexts. Recent empirical research shows that symmetric AI access in negotiations can yield 84.4% higher joint gains and substantially increased value creation (Rana, 2024), but these benefits depend critically on system reliability. This paper introduces Prescriptive Agent Scaffolding (PAS), a theoretical framework for building reliable AI negotiation agents through external augmentation rather than internal LLM modification. PAS addresses seven limitation categories-non-determinism, hallucinations, opaque reasoning, absence of persistent memory, inability to learn from errors, lack of world models, and logical inconsistencies-using mechanistic controls, structured processes, and specialized tools that compensate for inherent weaknesses while preserving LLM strengths. Grounded in cognitive science, systems theory, and hybrid AI principles, the framework provides a systematic methodology for constructing enterprise-grade negotiation support agents. Through analysis of an agent architecture currently in prototype development, the paper demonstrates how PAS principles translate into practical system design and outlines critical research questions requiring empirical validation.

title: Designing Effective Behavioral Change Strategies: An Evidence-Based Framework

detail.title: Designing Effective Behavioral Change Strategies: An Evidence-Based Framework
detail.abstract: Behavioral change remains a central challenge for organizations navigating digital transformation, operational improvement, and cultural evolution. This article synthesizes academic research and practitioner insights to present a systematic approach to designing behavioural change strategies grounded in the Fundamental Behaviour Influence Framework (FBIF). The framework positions behaviour as emerging from reciprocal interactions between extrinsic environments (social, work, cultural), intrinsic factors (biopsychological state, personality, readiness potential), and dynamic feedback loops. Drawing on contemporary research in organizational psychology, behavioural economics, and implementation science, the article examines how organizations can intervene at multiple leverage points-environmental redesign, intrinsic state modification, readiness enhancement, and feedback optimization-to achieve sustainable change. Evidence from healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, and technology sectors demonstrates practical applications across diverse contexts. The article concludes with strategic recommendations for building adaptive behavioural change capabilities that balance immediate performance needs with long-term organizational resilience.

title: Institutional Da'wah and Trust-Building in the Digital Era: Evidence from BAZNAS Lubuklinggau, Indonesia

detail.abstract: This study investigates how institutional da'wah strategies implemented by the National Zakat Agency (BAZNAS) of Lubuklinggau City contribute to strengthening public trust and enhancing muzakki participation in the digital era. Employing a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews, field observations, and institutional documentation. The findings indicate that BAZNAS integrates four interrelated strategies-educational, persuasive, collaborative, and digital-in managing da'wah activities. These approaches have significantly increased public awareness, transparency, and participation in zakat management. Digital innovation, particularly online zakat payment systems, social media engagement, and open financial reporting, has become a catalyst for building institutional trust and modernizing religious communication. Nonetheless, challenges such as limited zakat literacy and unequal access to technology persist, particularly in rural areas. The study concludes that adaptive, transparent, and trust-based institutional da'wah is crucial for ensuring sustainable religious engagement and maximizing zakat potential in Indonesia's digital transformation context.

title: Climate Change News Risk and Advertising Spending

detail.title: Climate Change News Risk and Advertising Spending

keywords: Climate Change News Risk. Advertising Expenditure

detail.abstract: We examine the effect of climate change news risk on corporate advertising spending. Using a novel measure of media-driven climate risk matched to firm-level advertising data, we find a robust negative relationship between climate news risk and advertising spending. Mechanism tests show that financial constraints mediate this relationship. The effect is stronger for firms with low stock market liquidity and high cash-flow volatility. We also find that domestic firms reduce their advertising spending relative to their multinational counterparts, which aligns with the idea that international operations provide diversification and stronger cash flow benefits that enhance firms' resilience to the effects of domestic climate risk shocks. The results remain consistent across different advertising measures, and after correcting for selection bias with a Heckman two-step method. We address endogeneity concerns through instrumental variable estimation. Our findings support the risk management hypothesis that firms proactively adjust their financial policies to mitigate the negative effects of rising climate risk exposure.

title: Game-Changer for Indian Arbitration Law! Supreme Court Steps in to Rewrite the Rules on Delay and Dysfunction

detail.title: Game-Changer for Indian Arbitration Law! Supreme Court Steps in to Rewrite the Rules on Delay and Dysfunction
detail.abstract:
In a landmark ruling, the Supreme Court of India dismantles an arbitral award that took nearly four years to arrive, only to leave the parties in deeper conflict. This case isn’t just about delay; it’s about the failure of arbitration to deliver justice, and the Court’s bold invocation of Article 142 to restore balance. If you’re a legal professional, arbitrator, or policy thinker, this judgment is a must-read for its implications on public policy, procedural fairness, and the future of dispute resolution in India.

The Supreme Court’s ruling in Lancor Holdings Ltd. v. Prem Kumar Menon is a watershed moment for Indian arbitration. In holding that unexplained delay and incomplete reasoning can vitiate an award under Sections 34(2)(b)(ii) & 34(2A), the Court has made one thing clear: arbitration in India must deliver timely, final, and equitable outcomes.

This judgment reinforces that arbitrators are not merely neutral observers but custodians of fairness whose orders must restore balance, not create fresh litigation. By setting aside a four-year-delayed, indecisive, and inequitable award, the Court safeguards commercial certainty and advances India's ambition to be an arbitration friendly jurisdiction.

detail.title: Design and Optimization of a Robust Vaccine Supply Chain with Defects and Waste under Uncertainty
detail.abstract: The recent COVID-19 pandemic triggered a surge in concern on the global vaccine supply chain (SC), emphasizing the urgent need for improved vaccine access. This lack of access has severely hindered efforts to control the outbreak and meet vaccine demand. Most of the existing literature on vaccine SC builds assumptions upon perfect vaccine units with demand uncertainty. However, frequently neglected imperfect and disrupted sustainable vaccine supply chain networks (VSCN) facing multiple uncertainties. To address these uncertainties and ensure optimal vaccine distribution a robust optimization approach is proposed. Additionally, a Lagrangian relaxation algorithm (LRA) is developed to alleviate the computational burden of the stochastic dynamic problem, while a priori probability bounds on constraint satisfaction are introduced to account for the decision-maker's risk attitude. Numerical experiments are conducted using an illustrative example to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model. The computational results indicate that incorporating uncertainties related to demand, inspection errors, and vaccine waste enables prompt responses to unexpected supply shortages, effectively meets the needs of healthcare centers, and enhances the network's resilience to future parameter deviations. Additionally, the results show that the model is capable of providing less conservative solutions. Additional managerial insights and potential avenues for future research are also discussed.

detail.abstract: The institutional framework for implementing performance management system in the Gauteng Province's Johannesburg and Tshwane Metropolitan Municipalities is covered in Chapter Three. Chapter 7 of the Constitution of 1996 establishes three categories for local government, specifically, local municipalities (Category B), districts (Category C), and metropolitan areas (Category A). Provincial municipalities, also known as metropolitans in each region, have sole jurisdiction over local government and legislation, according to the 2017 reports of the Statistics South Africa. They are found in significant, densely populated regions with stable, intricate, and varied economies. It is argued that the district municipalities are responsible for planning and allocating resources among the local municipalities and cooperating with other branches of government. The study used a literature and document review to compile information on performance management systems in South African municipalities. The study used secondary data to compile information. No interviews and questionnaires form part of the study, hence there was no human interaction recorded. The aim of the study is to explain what are the factors that may hamper the effective implementation of performance management system at local governance level. The study identifies various challenges linking to performance management such as training, commitment from higher management, awareness, cultural change, to state a few. Based on the findings, the article suggests various interventions to improve the implementation status quo of performance management systems.

title: The Future of Growth in a Resource-Rich State: Azerbaijan's Post-Oil Dilemma
affiliations: Economic Research Center (ERC)

detail.title: The Future of Growth in a Resource-Rich State: Azerbaijan's Post-Oil Dilemma
detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of Azerbaijan's economic trajectory over three decades of post-Soviet transformation, emphasizing the interplay between hydrocarbon dependence, fiscal fragility, and institutional weakness. Drawing upon national statistics, official budget data, and projections by international financial institutions-including the World Bank, IMF, EBRD, and ADB-the study traces macroeconomic dynamics from 1996 to 2025 and examines long-term sustainability prospects through 2050. The findings reveal that while hydrocarbon revenues have enabled rapid early growth and large-scale public investments, they have simultaneously entrenched structural vulnerabilities. Declining oil production, exchange-rate rigidity, weak diversification, and opaque fiscal governance have left the economy increasingly exposed to external shocks and domestic inefficiencies. Institutionally, Azerbaijan's governance environment has deteriorated, characterized by shrinking civic space, weakened judicial independence, and rising authoritarian control over economic and financial institutions. These systemic deficiencies have undermined investor confidence, constrained innovation, and reinforced monopolistic market structures. The study integrates macroeconomic, institutional, and geopolitical dimensions into a unified analytical framework, demonstrating that Azerbaijan's shortterm fiscal surpluses mask deeper mid-term vulnerabilities and long-term structural risks. World Bank long-term growth simulations project average annual GDP growth of only 0.5 percent between 2024 and 2050-insufficient to achieve high-income status within the century under current policy conditions. The paper concludes by identifying key reform priorities, including institutional modernization, fiscal transparency, exchangerate flexibility, and the promotion of innovation-driven non-oil growth, as essential for achieving sustainable and inclusive economic transformation in a post-oil future.
